source_documents.title: Monomeric Fluorescence of H‐Aggregates in a Series of 2‐(Hydroxyphenyl)benzoxazoles Derivatives

reference_evidence_units.quote: These aggregates exhibit intense fluorescence despite the prohibition imposed by Kasha’s rule.
reference_evidence_units.subject: HBOs 1a-1c
reference_evidence_units.statement: H-aggregates of the HBOs are strongly fluorescent.

reference_evidence_units.quote: This violation seems to result from the deactivation mechanism of the excited excitonic state in HBO H-aggregates, which involves, along with internal conversion, a photochemical channel induced by excited-state intramolecular proton transfer (ESIPT) rather than a radiative one.
reference_evidence_units.subject: HBOs 1a-1c
reference_evidence_units.statement: The excitonic state of the H-aggregate decays through ESIPT, giving monomeric keto emission.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The consequence of ESIPT is monomeric fluorescence from the keto forms of HBOs.
reference_evidence_units.subject: HBOs 1a-1c

reference_evidence_units.quote: This enhancement is due to intramolecular hydrogen bonds as well as the dense molecular packing of HBOs, which suppresses conformational transformations.
reference_evidence_units.subject: HBOs 1a-1c
reference_evidence_units.statement: Higher crystal quantum yields (0.81-0.91) are attributed to H-bonds and dense packing.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: The suppressed motion is not specified.
